title: Hermes: an all-in-one entropy tool
description: Hermes measures the entropy of a phase from molecular dynamics, term by term, and turns it into CALPHAD parameters. Configurational entropy over listed configurations keeps the zentropy core of pyzentropy 0.1.1 (N. L. E. Hew, Phases Research Lab, MIT license). The vibrational entropy of a crystal comes from MD positions, by compression (a clean-room implementation written from the preprint of Fisher and Hong, arXiv:2512.02221) or as Gaussian, less the entropy the atoms share, taken exactly from the crystal's translations; near melting it is carried up from a moderate temperature by the heat capacity of NPT runs. Also the quantum correction from the MD velocity spectrum, liquid entropy from partial pair distribution functions, and excess mixing entropy from composition fluctuations. Version 0.2.0 adds the terms atomic motion does not carry: the crystal-field entropy of lanthanide ions from measured levels, magnetic entropy and Gibbs energy by the Inden / Hillert-Jarl model, and electronic entropy from a density of states; these are checked against exact results only so far. Output: Redlich-Kister parameters as TDB lines, and mixing and formation (enthalpy, entropy, heat capacity) data as ESPEI datasets. Every route is checked against thermodynamic integration in pre-registered tests, all reported in docs/validation.md.
